title: Famulus Blueprint Schema Annotation Protocol
description: Metadata required on canonical typed blueprint schemas so schema files define authoring, hashing, and enforcement links.

schema-shape.description: Validate required fields, values, and unknown-field rejection through the selected JSON Schema.
schema-shape.creation: Render each typed document from its concrete schema and reject values outside that schema before graph construction.
schema-shape.template: Render every root and sidecar from its concrete typed schema.

enforcement.note: JSON Schema is the current acceptance component.

canonical-id.description: Validate skill, interface, and behavior-source IDs and namespaces.
canonical-id.creation: Use the canonical skill, interface, or behavior-source namespace required by the concrete schema.
canonical-id.template: Use example-skill for local IDs and references.source.policy for the repository behavior-source example.

enforcement.note: The validator accepts isolated repository fixtures through validate(repo_root).

root-directory-id.description: Require a typed skill root ID to equal its skill directory name.
root-directory-id.creation: Name blueprint.yaml with the exact directory skill ID.

enforcement.note: load_skill_blueprint_graph enforces root-directory identity.

version-pin.description: Require positive versions and exact edge-to-target version matches.
version-pin.creation: Use positive versions and pin every declared edge to the target node version.

enforcement.note: The relationship validator checks reachable fixture versions.

gateway-file.description: Require every authored node to name an existing regular file as its gateway.
gateway-file.creation: Name one file relative to the node ownership root and include it in the node's content patterns.
gateway-file.template: Create SKILL.md, _rtx/_runner.py, _cx/_command, and references/policy.md before validating the example graph.

enforcement.note: Typed graph loading and source validation require an existing regular gateway file included in content.

content-files.description: Resolve every content regex to the complete set of files owned by its node and require the gateway to match.
content-files.creation: Use node-relative regular expressions that match all and only the files belonging to the node.
content-files.template: Each example content list matches its gateway and any additional exclusively owned files.

enforcement.note: Graph and source validation compile content expressions, resolve matching files, and require gateway inclusion.

content-exclusive.description: Require every content file to have exactly one authored node owner.
content-exclusive.creation: Partition skill and repository files between authored nodes without overlapping content matches.
content-exclusive.template: The skill root owns SKILL.md while each sidecar owns its separate implementation or instruction files.

enforcement.note: Graph and source validation reject content files claimed by more than one authored node.

root-interface-edge.description: Require one canonical root and exactly one default LLM interface representation.
root-interface-edge.creation: Define default_interface inline in every version 3 skill root; version 2 readers retain legacy sidecar compatibility.

enforcement.note: The typed skill schema is the current acceptance component.

default-interface.description: Treat the inline default contract as the canonical skill.llm.default interface bound to SKILL.md.
default-interface.creation: Author the default contract under blueprint.yaml default_interface without a separate ID, gateway, content list, sidecar, or health record.
default-interface.template: Use blueprint.yaml#default_interface for the default LLM contract.

enforcement.note: Schema and graph normalization enforce one representation and root health folds the inline default into the skill.

relationship-edge.description: Resolve graph edges, target types, uniqueness, reachability, and cycles.
relationship-edge.creation: Declare only canonical, version-pinned graph edges with a target sidecar locator where required.
relationship-edge.template: The local root declares its four interface sidecars without duplicate edges.

enforcement.note: The relationship validator accepts the reachable local fixture.

access-control.description: Validate allow-all and caller allowlist behavior for cross-skill interface edges.
access-control.creation: Set allow_all_skills or enumerate the permitted caller skill IDs for cross-skill use.
access-control.template: The single-skill fixture has no cross-skill interface edge requiring an allowlist.

enforcement.note: The relationship validator enforces current access-control rules.

gateway-kind.description: Allow Python entrypoint files under _rtx and direct command files under _cx, never inline shell strings.
gateway-kind.creation: Use python-entrypoint for _rtx files and command-file for executable _cx files.
gateway-kind.template: The example has Python gateways and one command-file gateway.

enforcement.note: The machine-interface schema selects the allowed gateway forms.

dispatcher-argv-pattern.description: Validate dispatcher argument patterns without treating them as subsystem confinement.
dispatcher-argv-pattern.creation: Declare only caller-visible argv patterns and never use them as evidence of resource confinement.
dispatcher-argv-pattern.template: The example uses no optional argv pattern.

enforcement.note: The machine-interface schema validates declared pattern shape.

runtime-dependency.description: Validate declared runtime dependency applicability and required-interface platform support through the reachable interface closure.
runtime-dependency.creation: State interface support explicitly, list non-stdlib dependencies, use each dependency platform map to declare where each dependency applies, and never claim a platform absent from a required interface.
runtime-dependency.template: The example declares all platforms and no dependencies.

enforcement.note: The machine-interface schema validates dependency applicability-map shape, and the graph contract rejects platform claims not supported by required interfaces.

direct-io-description.description: Validate descriptive immediate IO while excluding it from certified contract hashes.
direct-io-description.creation: Describe immediate semantic IO without claiming subsystem confinement.
direct-io-description.template: The example uses empty reads, writes, and network lists.

enforcement.note: The source validator applies the typed direct_io schema and its descriptive, non-confinement contract.

filesystem-ownership.description: Validate machine and LLM file ownership and reader relationships.
filesystem-ownership.creation: Give each writable path one owner and enumerate any authorized readers.
filesystem-ownership.template: The example declares no owned filesystem paths.

enforcement.note: The source validator enforces typed filesystem ownership, reader authorization, and overlap rules.

behavior-source-edge.description: Require behavior-source edge targets, consumer-local reasons, and source-to-source edge typing.
behavior-source-edge.creation: Use a version-pinned behavior-source sidecar locator and state the consumer-local reason.
behavior-source-edge.template: The repository behavior-source sidecar is rendered as a schema-valid cross-root composition fixture.

enforcement.note: The relationship validator resolves version-pinned behavior-source edges, validates target types, and rejects duplicate or cyclic edges.

interface-body-use.description: Require typed LLM and behavior-source bodies to use declared canonical interface IDs instead of bare cross-skill names.
interface-body-use.creation: Name declared canonical interface IDs in bodies and never invoke a bare skill or direct _rtx/_cx path.
interface-body-use.template: The generated blocks are excluded from hand-authored body checks and the fixture body contains no undeclared reference.

enforcement.note: The dependency validator accepts isolated typed fixtures.

generated-contract-block.description: Require generated SKILL.md blueprint contract and interface blocks to match the canonical root and declared interfaces.
generated-contract-block.creation: Generate the contract block from the canonical root and generate the interface block from declared interfaces; do not hand-maintain either block.
generated-contract-block.template: template.yaml requires both generated SKILL.md blocks and the fixture writes both marker pairs.

enforcement.note: Blueprint and skill-body validators compare generated contract and interface blocks with the typed root and declared interfaces.

gateway-sidecar-naming.description: Derive each version 3 hidden sidecar name deterministically from its unique gateway file.
gateway-sidecar-naming.creation: For gateway P, use dirname(P)/.basename(P).blueprint.yaml; version 3 forbids shared gateways and qualified sidecars.
gateway-sidecar-naming.template: Keep the default inline and use _rtx/._runner.py.blueprint.yaml for the _rtx/_runner.py gateway.

enforcement.note: Graph loading enforces the unqualified sidecar path derived from each unique version 3 gateway.

content-tracked.description: Require every resolved content file to be tracked by the relevant Git commit.
content-tracked.creation: Use content patterns that resolve only to repository-relative files tracked by the captured commit.
content-tracked.template: The lifecycle fixture Git-adds SKILL.md, gateways, content files, sidecars, and the repository policy source.

enforcement.note: Source validation requires authored sidecars and resolved content files to be present in the Git index.

content-non-symlink.description: Require every resolved content file to be a regular file rather than a symlink.
content-non-symlink.creation: Resolve content from the owning node root and reject symlink components, symlink endpoints, and non-regular files; command gateways must also be executable under _cx.
content-non-symlink.template: The lifecycle fixture writes regular files and makes _cx/_command executable.

enforcement.note: Graph and source validation reject symlink components, symlink endpoints, non-regular content files, and invalid command-file placement or mode.

semantic-type.description: Classify the semantic role of the complete behavior-source artifact with the closed version 3 vocabulary.
semantic-type.creation: Choose policy, instructions, reference, configuration, preference, schema, template, example, checklist, or dataset.
semantic-type.template: The repository policy source uses semantic_type: policy.

enforcement.note: The behavior-source schema enforces the closed semantic-type vocabulary.

behavior-source-visibility.description: Restrict skill-local behavior sources to their declaring skill while making repository references visible to all skills.
behavior-source-visibility.creation: A node may reference its own skills/<skill>/ files or repository-root references/ files, never another skill's local behavior source; namespace ownership matches physical location.
behavior-source-visibility.template: template.yaml supplies references/.policy.md.blueprint.yaml as the repository-owned source example.

enforcement.note: Relationship validation permits declaring-skill local sources and repository references while rejecting direct edges to another skill's local source.

relationship-matrix.description: Allow only schema-declared edge types between typed blueprint node families.
relationship-matrix.creation: Use x-famulus.relationship_matrix as the complete source of allowed graph relations and target types.
relationship-matrix.template: The reachable fixture uses only edge and target-type combinations declared by the relationship matrix.

enforcement.note: The relationship validator loads the schema metadata matrix as the authoritative edge and target-type policy.

commit-backed-stamp.description: Require node and skill health records to carry one restorable Git source stamp for their resolved content files.
commit-backed-stamp.creation: Set source.vcs to git, source.commit to the captured full Git object ID, and source.input_paths to sorted repository-relative content files that are tracked, regular, non-symlink, and byte-identical in HEAD, index, and worktree.
commit-backed-stamp.template: No author template emits health records; health.schema.json defines source only for node-health and skill-health records.

enforcement.note: Artifact-health production and admission require authenticated node-local source metadata tied to a restorable Git commit.

canonical-pooled-review.description: Keep pooled review derived, generated, and non-authoritative with respect to the canonical blueprint graph and node health.
canonical-pooled-review.creation: Render a pooled review only from one canonical root, reachable typed sidecars, and authenticated health records; never use it to declare graph edges or replace node health.
canonical-pooled-review.template: The template has no pooled-review input because pooled review is generated after canonical graph and health validation.

enforcement.note: Pooled review generation and health admission use the exact canonical graph and admitted node records without affecting canonical health.

interface.document.closed@1.statement: No unknown, deprecated, profile, draft, call-family, or dispatcher-consequence fields are authored.

interface.identity.canonical@1.statement: Module, export, and local IDs and versions are canonical and unique.

interface.arguments.type-complete@1.statement: Every argument and recursive subtype has all kind-specific authored fields.

interface.arguments.defaults-valid@1.statement: Required, default, and fixed values are compatible and type-valid.

interface.arguments.io-linked@1.statement: Filesystem arguments and dynamic direct-I/O paths have exact bidirectional typed references.

interface.binding.total@1.statement: Every public value has one binding and every declared fixed parameter compiles.

interface.binding.unambiguous@1.statement: Binding positions and names are unique and contain no fixed, caller, or dispatcher-option collision or raw argv fragment.

interface.binding.dispatch-order@1.statement: The compiled binding has one positional-first, named-after terminal form.

interface.references.resolved@1.statement: Every schema, resource, I/O, output, outcome, helper, and verification reference resolves with the required type and version.

interface.outputs.structured@1.statement: Output IDs, channels, framing, types, schemas, cardinality, and empty meaning are usable.

interface.outputs.io-linked@1.statement: Every output resolves to a channel-compatible immediate direct-I/O write.

interface.outcomes.structured@1.statement: Outcome IDs, classes, signals, references, actions, and structural coverage are valid.

interface.execution.axes-consistent@1.statement: Effect and lifecycle axes admit exactly their applicable conditional blocks.

interface.execution.decisions-valid@1.statement: Tagged execution decisions use one allowed tag and satisfy retry and verification constraints.

interface.effects.io-consistent@1.statement: Effects and verification point to compatible declared I/O, outputs, helpers, and outcomes.

interface.effects.outcome-inverse@1.statement: Outcome effect lists and effect occurrence sets are exact inverses.

interface.ownership.authorized@1.statement: Writes are within shared or private authority and ownership scopes do not overlap.

interface.dependencies.direct@1.statement: Effective tools are exactly the direct module and interface union without sibling or transitive inheritance.

interface.dependencies.authorized@1.statement: Target IDs, versions, platforms, and caller permissions resolve and permit every edge.

interface.helpers.well-bound@1.statement: Helpers are direct, bounded, acyclic, type-compatible, safely routed, and contain no fixed secrets.

interface.sensitivity.transport-safe@1.statement: Secrets and credentials are absent from argv, fixed values, examples, and generated usage.

interface.direct-io.internal-path-safe@1.statement: Implicit temporary and log paths are relative, traversal-free, and confined.

interface.preconditions.structured@1.statement: Preconditions have stable IDs, checks, unmet outcomes, and caller actions.

interface.interaction.structured@1.statement: Interaction mode, channels, unattended outcome, timeout, and cancellation satisfy the selected mode.

interface.version.breaking-change@1.statement: Mechanically known breaking differences from the previous certified contract have a higher public version.

interface.injection.closed@1.statement: Projection contains only the consumer-selected exports, bounded helpers, and required definitions.

interface.injection.export-size-bounded@.statement: One export validation-equivalent projection is at most 12288 UTF-8 bytes without truncation.

interface.injection.consumer-size-bounde.statement: One consumer combined projection is at most 16384 UTF-8 bytes without truncation.

interface.gateway.accepts-binding@1.statement: Representative, empty, boundary, and invalid invocations reach the declared parser outcomes.

interface.gateway.enforces-fixed-values@.statement: Callers cannot override or duplicate fixed parameters.

interface.outputs.conform@1.statement: Captured streams satisfy declared channel, encoding, framing, type, and schema.

interface.outcomes.conform@1.statement: Fixtures for applicable terminal cases produce declared signals and references.

interface.lifecycle.conform@1.statement: Finite and long-running fixtures satisfy declared termination, readiness, stop, and cleanup behavior.

interface.effects.conform@1.statement: Controlled probes observe declared effects and confirmation evidence.

interface.protected-file.conform@1.statement: Covered fixtures demonstrate no-follow and owner-private handling on every supported platform claimed by a protected-file export.

interface.boundary.covered@1.statement: The injected seam and sandbox demonstrate interception of every boundary used by effect or absence claims.

interface.semantic.single-operation@1.statement: The export is one coherent operation and not a hidden mode family.

interface.semantic.argument-independent@.statement: No public argument changes another argument's meaning, legality, authorization, effects, or interpretation.

interface.semantic.descriptions-exact@1.statement: Module, interface, argument, output, and outcome prose accurately describes behavior.

interface.semantic.outcomes-complete@1.statement: Caller-visible terminal and uncertain-completion cases are complete and nonmisleading.

interface.semantic.io-complete@1.statement: Direct I/O, effects, ownership, helpers, and direct tools omit no relevant behavior.

interface.semantic.sensitivity-correct@1.statement: Sensitivity classifications and transport choices match the substantive data.

interface.semantic.execution-accurate@1.statement: Consistency, atomicity, concurrency, idempotency, partial effects, rollback, lifecycle, and verification claims are true.

interface.semantic.invocation-compatible.statement: Fixed and public ordering and encoding preserve the gateway operation's meaning.

interface.semantic.preconditions-complet.statement: All material preconditions and caller actions are represented.

interface.semantic.interaction-accurate@.statement: Prompting, unattended behavior, timeout, cancellation, and warning claims match behavior.

interface.semantic.version-compatible@1.statement: Ambiguous public-contract changes are classified correctly as breaking or nonbreaking.
